output.brief: The evidence points away from the new CDN and toward the smart-TV app 5.2 release. Since 9 October, smart-TV 5.2 sessions stall about 5.9% of viewing time. Every other client (older TV app, web, iOS/Android) on the same Tessaline CDN and the same ISPs stays at 0.6–0.7%. Before the cutover, every client and ISP was normal. The rise began on 9 October, when both the CDN cutover and 5.2 went live, and the CDN change alone can't explain why only the new app is hit. Congestion at ISPs and the handball launch also don't fit, because the stalls started before the launch and only one app is affected. I'm fairly confident (~85–90%). The link between buffering and the October cancellation rise is not established: the 1 October price rise is a competing explanation, and the exit survey has no quality option. Next steps: don't send the SLA notice, withhold fees or roll back the CDN. Don't mute the alert. Revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour in Kestria and hold the wider rollout. Add app-version and device breakdowns to the dashboard and alerts. Hold the free-month offer until the cancellation cause is clearer.
